MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron sits at delimiter/boundary positions inside enumerations and spec lists — commas, coordinating "and", closing parentheses, and short function words like "the" separating consecutive list items (country names, measurements, dB/Hz specs) — rather than on any content word; nearly identical list-separator tokens can also strongly suppress it, so it is essentially a list-punctuation/conjunction position detector.

L12·N7222unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the token that immediately precedes a passive/past-participle predicate — typically the head noun of the subject or the auxiliary/verb right before the participle ("body|was found", "forces|carried out by", "they are|incorporated", "is only saved|from") — i.e., the boundary just before a passive construction; it is strongly suppressed by the agentive "by" itself and by object nouns of active verbs.
